newsitem.title: GERMANY: German roasters seek some nearby coffee.
newsitem.headline: German roasters seek some nearby coffee.

text.p: German coffee roasters are looking for some spot supply to fill gaps in their cover, traders said on Monday.
But activities in more distant months were stifled by volatile futures and the expectation of a tight supply scenario throughout 1997.
This kept prices high and origin offers slim.
"Consumers still need some cover but they don't like buying outright at current prices," one trader said.
New York March arabicas on Friday ended at 205.0 cents/lb, up 3.00, and May at 186.35 cents, up 4.10.
Consumers were targetting 178 cents on May for purchases but the contract's near term trading range was broadly seen at 179-195.
Roasted coffee price rises at most German plants, which came into effect last Monday, were not yet felt in the retail market as wholesalers and supermarkets had hoarded supplies at the old price.
They were aiming to make competitive offers in the run-up to Easter on March 30, when consumption peaks seasonally, and in order to give consumers a chance to stock up on coffee relatively cheaply.
Roasters may wish to announce another round of price increases because the one mark per 0.5 kg increase was far from fully reflecting higher green coffee costs, traders said.
"Further price rises could be on their way for the time after Easter when consumption is expected to fall anyway," one said.
In the domestic import market, Latin American arabica prices were $4-7 down on the week per 50 kg fob, with Brazils at $194, off $6.
But Kenyans rose $5 to $300 on export demand.
Vietnam robustas were unchanged at $76.50 per 50 kg cif. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
